rules: Show the Korean line in Hangul before any romanization.
Use short natural English for every visible explanation, meaning note, grammar or politeness rule, practice instruction, and CTA guidance.

Allow Hangul on cards only for what the learner hears or says, the exact target phrase or its Korean components, and limited pronunciation practice. Do not write learner-facing explanations in Korean.
Use romanization only as a pronunciation aid and never as the only way to read the lesson.
Teach polite everyday Korean by default and name any speech-level contrast explicitly.
Do not assume Korean cultural knowledge or address a Korean-only audience.
reviewQuestions: Can an English-speaking beginner understand every explanation and instruction without reading Korean?
Does every visible Hangul string belong to real dialogue, the target phrase, a phrase component, or pronunciation practice?
Does Hangul remain more prominent than romanization?
Is every Korean line natural in the stated real-life scene?
Is the pronunciation help useful without pretending to replace listening practice?
